newsitem.title: USA: U.S. WEEKLY CASH LUMBER REVIEW - AUG 8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. WEEKLY CASH LUMBER REVIEW - AUG 8.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - More active trading boosted sales at mills in Canada and the West, but demand for Southern Pine continued to trail production, Random Lengths said in its end-week market update. Prices finished mixed, with the Randon Lengths Framing Lumber Composite down $1 for the week.

Most orders came from dealers and distributors replenishing inventories they had allowed to run down in previous weeks. Many producers were slow to raise prices, focusing instead of reducing inventories and extending order files, Random Lengths said.
In the South, where treating plants had the end of their peak selling season in sight, buyers stuck to strict just-in-time purchasing.
With mills' vacations and maintenance shutdowns mostly completed, traders expressed concern over the market's long-term ability to support current production.
Some sources speculated that improved sales were driven in part by railcar shortages at U.S. mills, with customers mistaking an inability to ship for a tightening of supplies.

A well-drained pipeline that forced buyers to play catch-up magnified the quicker pace and diverted more business to reloads and distributors. News Thursday afternoon that labor negotiations had reached a settlement in the B.C. Northern Interior came too late to affect trading.
Rising futures prices spurred some buying. Wholesalers took small long positions after covering shorts, but were inclined to turn the wood quickly.

A heat wave in California accompanied by scattered brush fires didn't have much impact, but gave traders something to talk about. Board prices remained weak, though sales got a boost when some buyers stepped in to clean up lower-priced stock. Radius edge decking continued its record run in the South, but the rate of price increased moderated slightly.
